name: Easel
text: To achieve our goal of designing the look of the AI website/product, I propose that we start by creating a mood board to capture the essence and aesthetic we want to convey. This is the best option because it allows us to visually explore and express the desired tone, style, and atmosphere, which will guide our subsequent design decisions. By focusing on a mood board first, we're accepting the trade-off of delaying the creation of more concrete design elements, such as layouts and interfaces, but this will ultimately ensure that our final design is cohesive and effective. This approach will also enable us to learn from Eitan's picks and incorporate his taste into our design.

name: Squint
text: I'm not convinced that a mood board is the best place to start, as it may lead to a subjective and vague representation of our design goals, potentially causing misunderstandings down the line. A more concrete approach might be to identify the specific design elements that Eitan's picks have in common, and use those as a foundation for our design. To settle this, I'd like to see a comparison of the benefits and drawbacks of each approach, as well as some examples of successful designs that have used mood boards versus more structured methods.

name: Easel
text:
I propose we start by **copying the exact color palette and typography from Eitan’s three strongest picks**—no mood board, no vague vibes. This gives us a clear, reusable system we can test in real layouts tomorrow. The trade-off is that we might miss some subtle texture or animation cues, but those can come later once we lock the core look.

text: I'm still not sold on copying the exact color palette and typography from Eitan's picks, as it may result in a lack of originality and potentially infringe on existing design copyrights. name: Chroma
text: DECISION: We will create a custom design language inspired by Eitan's picks, rather than copying them, to ensure originality and avoid potential copyright issues, and Easel will own the delivery of this unique visual identity that still captures the essence of Eitan's style.
